title: ctsegdose-core: anatomy-weighted CTDIvol from routine CT metadata, using deep-learning organ segmentation
description:
A Python package (MIT) that computes an anatomy-weighted CTDIvol index from routine CT DICOM metadata and automated organ segmentation: the whole-scan CTDIvol scaled by a dimensionless, organ-specific weight formed from the recorded per-slice tube current over that organ's segmented longitudinal extent. It also reports organ volume and attenuation-derived estimated organ mass.

The quantity is not new — it is the organ-specific weighted CTDIvol of Khatonabadi et al. (2013) and Tian et al. (2015). What this software provides is an open, end-to-end implementation that runs from archived DICOM alone, with contours obtained at inference.

It is not an estimate of absorbed organ dose. The index describes longitudinal tube-current modulation only, and does not account for scatter, irradiation from outside the segmented extent, angular modulation, organ depth and attenuation, or radiation transport. No organ-dose coefficient table is redistributed, and the software refuses to emit a dose in milligray without one.

No imaging data is redistributed. The public series analysed are identified in data/PROVENANCE.json by collection, collection DOI, Series Instance UID and licence, and can be re-fetched from The Cancer Imaging Archive by following docs/REPRODUCING_DATA.md.
